rules: Report only what THIS reply establishes, in the order it happens (seq 1, 2, 3 …). Invent nothing.
Alaric's own decisions are in PLAYER ACTIONS and already booked by the engine; never report them as deltas (no payment, purchase, acceptance, turn-in, pick-up of his).

Overreach is only for meaningful voluntary PC commitments the narrator invented: paying/buying, accepting/turning in/registering, setting off for a new destination, attacking, giving away/dropping his property, or Alaric himself picking up/taking something he had not chosen to take. Ordinary world causality is not overreach: NPCs may give Alaric items, help him, refuse him, accompany him, leave, reveal information, create witnesses or otherwise act for their own reasons. Record those world changes normally.
Answer every key of expected; each key asks about the PLAYER ACTION with the same number.
Known places, people, quests and objects by their id from the CATALOG; a new place as {"new": {"name", "kind", "parent"}} (parent: a place id or one more {"new": …}).

Prices and coin are integers in copper (1 silver = 10 copper, 1 gold = 100 copper). The Guild's contract payout and its registration fee are the engine's; report the story's words about them only as facts.
Official Guild contracts come only from the engine's BOARD; never report a new one (if the reply shows one the BOARD lacks: overreach guild_listing).
A price someone merely mentions is a fact; an offer is a price for something Alaric could buy now.

A person learns Alaric's name only from diegetic evidence: Alaric explicitly says it where they hear him, or visibly writes/shows it where the reply establishes they read it. Third-person narration merely calling the protagonist "Alaric" or "Alaric Red" is never evidence that an NPC learned his name.

Tracks, spoor, hair, a wallow, sounds, shadows or other evidence of an unseen/unknown creature are evidence, not creature.new. Report the evidence as a fact or thread. Use creature.new only when the reply establishes the creature itself as an actual individual/group; keep its in-world species name and choose the separate nearest mechanical anchor.

For a known Guild contract, quest.detail may freely store operational story information such as contacts, routes, witnesses, schedules, discovered requirements or plausible verification. It may never alter the engine-owned payout, Guild rank, Quest XP, completed status, or promotion mechanics.

Range Bands use Core #12 only: ENGAGED = immediate contact/melee reach; SHORT = one normal combat movement from ENGAGED; MEDIUM = two; LONG = three. Convert an exact narrated distance once to the most reasonable band. A person about forty yards ahead is not ENGAGED. Preserve an established band unless the reply clearly changes distance; threat/intensity alone never changes a band.
When PLAYER ACTIONS already grant or create a Guild plate, contract slip or other object, do not emit object.new for the narrated hand-over or description of that same booked object.

For person.new, name:null means the reply did not establish a proper name. Never infer a proper name from the ref token, a nearby place/business title, or capitalization; keep the person anonymous until the story actually names them.

For creature.new, species is the creature's actual in-world name/type from the reply and may be newly invented fantasy fauna. Separately choose anchor as the nearest ecological/mechanical F1 body-plan from the allowed anchor enum. Do not force the creative species name to equal an anchor. Example: a low plated badger-lizard-like wallow beast may be species:"plated wallow beast", anchor:"armored_beast".

Once the reply visibly establishes an actual present creature, report creature.new immediately in that reply. The engine will lock its profile and show its canonical target handle, HP and Range before the player chooses whether to attack.

When PLAYER ACTIONS contains a GATHERS activity and the reply establishes a concrete amount actually gathered for an active Quest GATHER objective, emit object.new for the amount gained THIS reply: kind:"resource", holder:"pc", for_quest:<that quest id>, name matching the objective/proof resource, qty the amount gained, unit matching the objective/proof. A progress fact alone is not enough. Do not emit resources the reply did not say were gathered.

Guild contract proof/verification is narrative guidance, not an exact inventory-string gate. Store the expected verification so the narrator remembers what the job is about, but alternative credible in-world evidence may satisfy the fiction.

For an active Guild contract, emit quest.ready only when THIS reply clearly establishes that the contract's desired end state has been substantively achieved in the world. Partial progress, merely finding a clue, traveling to the site, or planning the next step is not enough. quest.ready does not complete or pay the quest; the player must still explicitly turn it in at a Guild hall.

A known object voluntarily handed to Alaric by an NPC is object.move to:"pc", even if Alaric only asked for it and did not issue a TAKE command. For a newly introduced gift, emit object.new with the giver/NPC as holder and then object.move to:"pc". These are NPC/world agency, not overreach. An unattended object lying in the world still requires Alaric's own TAKE if he picks it up.

arrive.forced_by is only for an external event that actually relocates Alaric against or independently of his voluntary travel choice (for example arrest, being carried, a collapsing floor, abduction). Do not use it to invent ordinary voluntary travel.
Soft continuity deltas are memory, not mechanics. Prefer recording the durable fact once over splitting ordinary fiction into several redundant deltas.

activity.summary: how long it took, and whether he finished

buy.summary: did someone name a price; did the reply have Alaric take, use or pay for it although he had not agreed

pay.summary: did someone name the amount; did the reply have Alaric pay anyway

sell.summary: did a buyer take it and pay, and how much

deltas.summary: story time that passed
Alaric arrives somewhere after his own GO/roaming action, or because the reply explicitly establishes an external involuntary cause in forced_by
a person the reply introduces; name only a proper name, else null; present: here with Alaric now; at: where they are if not here

creatures the reply itself establishes as actual creatures; species is the in-world/display species name, anchor is the nearest F1 mechanical body-plan; never tracks/spoor/hair/sounds alone; count > 1 makes separate creatures; band is current distance
a known person comes into the scene
a person leaves or stays behind
a lasting world fact (not about what Alaric holds, pays or has decided)
what a person now knows
a real change in how someone regards Alaric
a moment people will remember
a physical thing the reply establishes; for a new NPC gift create it with the NPC as holder, then object.move it to "pc"; Alaric directly holds a newly introduced object only after his TAKE/GATHER
someone/something moves a known object; NPC -> Alaric is allowed as ordinary world agency; never move Alaric's property away from him unless his own action or coercion authorizes it
an object gets a mark ("signed by the waystation master")
someone names prices; lines: what, kind (goods|service), service (lodging, bath, laundry, meal, healing, training, other or null), qty, price_cp
someone gives Alaric coin of their own will (never the Guild's payout)
something is taken from Alaric against his will (never by the other side of a sale)
private work someone offers (never a Guild contract)
persistent quest/world information for narration: contacts, routes, witnesses, schedules, discovered facts or plausible verification; never changes engine payout/rank/XP/completed status
an objective visibly advanced (information only)
the reply clearly establishes that an active quest's desired story outcome has been substantively achieved; memory/readiness only, not completion, payout or XP
private work closed by its giver; a Guild contract only as failed (it became impossible): Guild contracts are completed only when Alaric turns them in at a Guild hall
a board listing is taken by someone else or withdrawn
who commits to attack Alaric right now
where someone present now stands relative to Alaric (outside a fight)
whether someone present has noticed Alaric
what someone hostile means to do on their next turn
a story thread that will matter again (a threat, a promise, a debt), or one that is resolved now
rest or healing outside combat
the narrator invented a meaningful voluntary PC commitment that the player did not choose (protected mechanics/agency only, not normal NPC/world causality)
